Photograph: Ida Marie Odgaard/Reuters View image in fullscreen Left to right: Thomas Ahrenkiel, the head of the Danish defence intelligence service; Jeppe Bruus, the defence minister, and Michael Hyldgaard, the chief of defence, at the release of the intelligence report in Copenhagen. Photograph: Ida Marie Odgaard/Reuters Nato Russia could attack a Nato country within months, Danish intelligence says Warning comes hours after Poland says fire at Starlink satellite station was ‘act of sabotage’ Pjotr Sauer in Kyiv Thu 24 Sep 2026 12.05 EDT Last modified on Thu 24 Sep 2026 12.22 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Russia could launch a limited military attack against a Nato country in the coming months, Danish intelligence said, in one of the starkest warnings yet by western security services. In a report published on Thursday, the Danish defence intelligence service warned of a “low but growing risk” that Russia could launch long-range strikes on Nato infrastructure supporting Ukraine , or carry out a limited incursion into a neighbouring country with a small number of troops, potentially operating without insignia. The report came hours after a fire at a Starlink satellite station in central Poland that local authorities described as an “act of sabotage”. Krzysztof Gawkowski, the deputy prime minister of Poland, said the blaze, which broke out overnight in the Masovian voivodeship, had been “deliberately designed to disable the station”, disrupting internet access for a number of institutions, including the Ukrainian military. View image in fullscreen The Starlink station in Wola Krobowska, Poland, April 2026. Photograph: Pleiades Neo © Airbus DS 2026/Reuters Gawkowski said it had not been established who ​was responsible for the fire, but that “many signs suggest this aligns with Russia’s new ‌doctrine ⁠of attack. “While everything is operational today, we must recognise, as prime minister [Donald] Tusk recently noted, that this is an element of hybrid warfare,” he said. Starlink has become a key part of Ukraine’s military communications, and the incident comes amid a spate of suspected Russian sabotage operations across European infrastructure supporting Ukraine. Earlier this month, Germany publicly blamed Russia for an attempted drone attack on Leipzig/Halle airport, while a series of other incidents – including fires at drone factories and sabotage targeting rail infrastructure – have also been investigated for possible links to Moscow. Russia has denied involvement in such attacks. European spy chiefs warn Moscow is planning more decisive action against Nato Read more In recent weeks, several European intelligence chiefs have warned that Russia may be preparing more assertive actions to test Nato countries’ commitment to supporting Ukraine, though officials differ over how imminent such a move may be. Russia is expected to intensify its hybrid attacks against European countries with “greater consequences” for those targeted in the coming months, the Danes warned, including “destructive cyber-attacks that cripple societal functions as well as sabotage attacks that carry a high risk of casualties”. A source familiar with Moscow’s thinking agreed that Russia was likely to step up its hybrid attacks. “Russian military top command is convinced some Nato countries are directly involved in the war against Russia – not just by supplying Ukraine with weapons and intelligence, but by helping to guide missiles and drones,” the source said, speaking on condition of anonymity. “They therefore believe Nato is already waging a hybrid war against Russia, and that Russia has the right to respond in kind,” the source added. “Hybrid attacks” are broad terms generally used to describe non-military tactics aimed at pressuring or destabilising an adversary, including cyber-attacks, sabotage and disinformation. The aim of Russia’s actions would be to divert European resources away from supporting Ukraine, and deepen divisions within Nato if the alliance failed to agree on a collective response, the report added. The service believes it remained “highly unlikely” that Russia would launch an outright invasion of a Nato country, but notably said it “cannot be ruled out”. The Danish services said Russia could seek to test Nato’s article 5, which commits members to collective defence. They warned there was “a risk that Russia assesses that the Nato countries will not respond collectively”, particularly if Moscow believes the US is unable or unwilling to support its European allies in a potential war with Russia. There have been ongoing jitters among Nato members over whether the alliance’s most powerful member, the US, would come to Europe’s defence under Donald Trump in the event of a Russian attack. Questions over unity within Europe are also growing. Last week, Slovakia’s prime minister, Robert Fico, who has maintained close ties with the Kremlin, cast doubt on his country’s commitment to Nato’s collective defence principle, saying he did not want Slovakia drawn into a military conflict “because of some article 5”. Speaking at the UN general assembly on Wednesday, Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia continued to threaten countries beyond Ukraine, including Moldova, Poland and the Baltic states, while showing “no respect” for the sovereignty of countries in the south Caucasus and central Asia. “The more freedom Putin has to act, the more dangerous the world becomes for everyone else,” he said. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/alerta-aeria.text: Un mesaj RO-Alert privind posibile incursiuni de drone a fost emis duminică, la puţin timp după miezul nopţii, pentru pentru zona de nord şi de est a judeţului Tulcea. Două avioane F-16 au fost ridicate de la Baza Fetești pentru verificări. MApN anunță că nu au fost înregistrate pătrunderi în spațiul aerian național. ACTUALIZARE 10:00 MAPN a anunțat duminică dimineața că „în cursul nopții de sâmbătă spre duminică, 21 spre 22 noiembrie, a fost semnalată o țintă aeriană la 63 de kilometri nord-est de localitatea Vâlcove, Ucraina”. Două F-16 ale Forțelor Aeriene Române au decolat de la Baza 86 Aeriană Fetești. Potrivit sursei citate, „Centrul Național Militar de Comandă (nucleu) a notificat Inspectoratul General pentru Situații de Urgență în vederea instituirii măsurilor de alertare a populației din zona de nord a județului Tulcea, iar la ora 00.46 a fost transmis un mesaj RO-Alert”. Nu au fost raportate pătrunderi în spațiul aerian național. „A fost transmis un mesaj RO-ALERT pentru zona de nord şi est a judeţului Tuclea la ora 00:46”, a anunțat ISU Tulcea. Locuitorii din zonele vizate au fost sfătuiţi să se adăpostească sau să rămână în case, departe de geamuri. „ALARMA AERIANA (POSIBILA INCURSIUNE DE DRONE). Pastrati-va calmul! Adapostiti-va in beciuri sau adaposturi de protectie civila. In lipsa unui adapost, ramaneti in interiorul casei, departe de geamuri si pereti exteriori”, scria în mesaj. La ora 02:16, alerta aeriană a încetat. „Nu au fost solicitări ori probleme raportate”, a transmis ISU Tulcea. Urmărește știrile Digi24.ro și pe Google News

Subscribe Fall Out Boy presale code searches now point to Wednesday, Nov. 11, when artist pre-sales begin for The Twilight of the Punks Tour. The general on-sale follows on Thursday, Nov. 12, giving ticket buyers a narrow two-day window before demand spills into the broader market. - Advertisement - Fall Out Boy announced the 36-city worldwide run in its 25th year as a band, and the route includes a 21-date North American stretch in 2027. The timeline is the part readers need most: early access starts first, then the wider sale opens the next day. Pete Wentz and Soldier Field Pete Wentz said the band will play Chicago’s Soldier Field on July 24, one of the clearest anchor dates in the North American run. That single stop gives the tour a visible Midwest marker inside a schedule that begins July 13 in Arlington, Texas, and closes Aug. 26 in Portland, Oregon. Wentz also said Joe Trohman will be at the shows, which matters because the lineup around a stadium tour is part of the draw for buyers deciding whether to act in the presale window or wait for the public sale. The tour’s scale makes timing part of the product. The Twilight of the Punks Tour The Twilight of the Punks Tour opens the European and U.K. leg on May 17 at Prague’s O2 Arena, then moves into the North American dates later in the summer. The Offspring, Good Charlotte, and the Story So Far are opening for most of the North American run, so the ticket window is not just about access to Fall Out Boy but also about the full bill attached to those dates. - Advertisement - Wentz pushed back on the implication built into the title itself, saying, “This is not a farewell tour” and adding, “I do always think that at some point it’s the last thing you make, and it should be important. [But] this is not it. This is not what I’m saying at all.” That leaves the title as branding, not a retirement signal, and keeps the sale focused on a tour that is still being sold as an active chapter. What buyers should do The practical move is simple: have the artist presale access ready before Wednesday, Nov. 11, then be prepared for the public on-sale on Thursday, Nov. 12. The presale code itself has not been disclosed in the available details, so anyone trying to buy early will need the access method that accompanies the artist presale rather than assuming the sale is open to everyone. The new song “Aces” also sits beside the announcement, with Patrick Stump singing, “Keep the fire alive” and “through trying times, through the slow decay and the rapid decline.” For buyers, that means the tour is being sold alongside fresh material, a long route, and a 2027 calendar that already stretches from Prague to Portland.
